title: Machine breakdowns per week
intro: A plant's maintenance records give the distribution of X, the number of machine breakdowns in a week, from 0 to 4. The data below list each value x with its probability P(x). Calculate the expected number of breakdowns per week, the variance and the standard deviation. Give each to two decimals or more.

Mean.says: That is the plain average of the five x values. Weight each x by its probability: μ = Σ x·P(x).

Variance.says: You subtracted μ from E[X²]. Subtract μ², the square of the mean: σ² = E[X²] − μ².

StandardDeviation.says: That is the variance. The standard deviation is its square root.

hints: μ = Σ x·P(x): multiply each x by its probability and add the five products.
Find E[X²] = Σ x²·P(x) the same way, then σ² = E[X²] − μ². Square the mean before you subtract.
σ is the square root of σ². There is no n or n − 1 to divide by: the probabilities already do the weighting.
